summary: Trevor Leggett worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied law at King's College London (~1931–1934) and served as Head of the Japanese Service at the BBC (~1946–1970).

Trijang Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Sherab Gyatso, served as a teacher at Ganden Shartse Monastery, and taught Tenzin Gyatso (14th Dalai Lama), Zong Rinpoche, Thubten Yeshe, and Thubten Zopa Rinpoche.

Troy Organ was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1939–1941). He held posts at the University of Akron (~1944–1946), Chatham University (~1946–1947), Parsons College (~1947–1954), and Ohio University (1954).
Trung Huynh works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of the West, where he was supervised by Darui Long (attested 2016).

Trungram Gyaltrul Rinpoche specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1997–2004) under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under Thomas Burke (attested 2004).

Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (1999–2004). He completed postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University and held a post at Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang works in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Village, and the University of Glasgow (1987). He served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Village and became Instructor in Tibetan at Oxford University in 2001.
Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche and at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Tsering Shakya specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at SOAS University of London (~1978–1992), where he later held a post (~1990–2007), before becoming a Professor at the University of British Columbia (~2007).

Tsoknyi Rinpoche is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Adeu Rinpoche, and taught Adam Pearcey.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Kyoto University, University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University. Supervised by Christopher I. Beckwith and Tatsuo Nishida, among others, he served as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University (~1994–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1956–1967). He lectured at Rissho University (~1969–1985) and served as President of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1975–2019) and Reiyūkai (~1976–2019).
Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013). She was supervised by K. L. Dhammajoti and also studied under Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who attended Toyama Chubu High School (~1967–1970). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1980–1994) and the University of Tokyo (~1994–2017).

Tsultrim Allione works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Abo Rinpoche, Chögyam Trungpa, and Namkhai Norbu, earned a master's at Antioch University (~1980–1982), and founded Tara Mandala.

Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

Tsultrim Kelsang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the International Buddhist Association (attested 1973), Otani University (attested 1984–2002), and Ryukoku University (2015).

Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962–1972) and held academic posts at Doshisha University (~1978–1995) and Kyoto University as Professor (~1995–2006).
Tsutomu Hatai worked in Indology and related fields. Succeeding Hiroshi Maruyama, he served as president (会長) of Ayurveda Kenkyūkai (attested 1987).
Tsutomu Horio is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Keiji Nishitani. He served as a Professor at Otani University (attested 1990).
